query: Single-phase ZrB2 benefits from strong Zr–B and B–B interactions and a high melting point, but it requires preparation temperatures above 2300 °C and does not readily meet application requirements on its own. Earlier studies sought to lower the required temperature, yet the resulting materials remained vulnerable to high-temperature oxidation or liquid plating-metal corrosion, while reported preparation temperatures generally remained above 1700 °C. Under the constraints of lower-temperature manufacture, adequate strength and structural integrity, oxidation durability, and prolonged service in a liquid plating bath, what single intervention could overcome these limitations? Provide one hypothesis specifying the intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome compared with single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens, applicable preparation and service boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment evaluating final body quality, structural integrity, oxidation, and liquid-metal corrosion that would falsify the hypothesis if its predictions were not observed.

generation.hypothesis: Alloying ZrB2 with a complementary set of metal diborides to form a high‐entropy boride (e.g. equiatomic HfB2, ZrB2, TaB2, NbB2, and TiB2) will enable densification at lower processing temperatures while simultaneously enhancing high‐temperature oxidation and liquid-metal corrosion resistance.
generation.intervention: Modify the composition by introducing additional metal diboride components to form a high-entropy diboride (e.g. (Hf0.2Zr0.2Ta0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2)B2), enabling a single-phase, chemically disordered microstructure.
generation.conditions: Fabrication via spark plasma sintering at reduced temperatures (~1700–1800 °C) with subsequent exposure to high-temperature oxidation (up to ~1500 °C) and corrosive liquid plating-metal environments.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a single-phase high-entropy diboride microstructure that promotes lower-temperature densification and forms a complex, multicomponent oxide scale at high temperature.
generation.mechanism: The increased configurational entropy in the high-entropy system lowers the sintering activation energy, allowing densification at reduced temperature. Simultaneously, the chemically disordered lattice hinders rapid oxygen and metal cation diffusion, which leads to the formation of a protective, multi-component oxide scale that improves oxidation durability and resistance to liquid-metal corrosion.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to conventional single-phase ZrB2 (fabricated above 2300 °C) and prior lower-temperature specimens, the high-entropy diboride fabricated at ~1700–1800 °C is expected to exhibit at least comparable mechanical strength and structural integrity while showing enhanced oxidation resistance and lower corrosion rates in a liquid plating-metal service environment.
generation.baseline: Single-phase ZrB2 manufactured at >2300 °C and lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens that, while processed at ~1700 °C, suffer from poorer oxidation and corrosion resistance.
generation.boundary: The intervention is applicable for processing temperatures up to about 1800 °C and service conditions featuring high temperature (up to ~1500 °C) and exposure to liquid plating metals; outside these boundaries, phase stability and protective scale formation may differ.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of improvements in oxidation and liquid-metal corrosion resistance is uncertain and will depend on the precise alloy composition and processing parameters, requiring optimization.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare three sets of samples: (i) conventional single-phase ZrB2 processed at >2300 °C, (ii) ZrB2 processed at a lower temperature (~1700 °C) without alloying, and (iii) the high-entropy diboride (e.g. (Hf0.2Zr0.2Ta0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2)B2) processed at ~1700–1800 °C. Subject all samples to standardized high-temperature oxidation tests in flowing dry air and corrosion tests in a liquid plating-metal environment. Characterize densification, microstructure, hardness, oxide scale composition, and corrosion rate.
measurements: Density measurements and microstructural imaging (SEM, XRD)
Weight change and oxide phase analysis post-oxidation
Quantitative corrosion rate evaluation in a liquid metal bath
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the high-entropy diboride does not demonstrate statistically significant improvements in densification, mechanical strength, oxidation resistance, and liquid-metal corrosion resistance compared to both the conventional high-temperature ZrB2 and the lower-temperature, non-alloyed ZrB2, then the hypothesis is falsified.
